# Havlek

> Havlek (legal name Hong Marketing Inc.) is a Vancouver, Canada software studio
> that builds AI products for clients and ships its own. Its consumer product is
> Photo to Video, an iOS app that turns a photo or a text prompt into an
> AI-generated video. Its developer product is Video Pipeline, a package of AI
> agent skills that takes a news story from topic selection to a finished,
> captioned video file.

Contact: info@havlek.ca · Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

## Photo to Video (iOS app)

An iPhone app that generates video from a still photo, a pair of frames, several
reference images, or a text prompt. Free to download. **No subscription** — you
buy credits only when you generate something, and credits do not expire.

- Platform: iOS (iPhone). No Android or web version.
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6788599776
- Product page: https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/
- Price: free to install; consumable credit packs via in-app purchase (150, 500,
  1200 or 2500 credits). There is no monthly or annual plan.
- Account: none required to start. Sign-in is only needed to buy credits.
- Privacy: submitted photos are sent to a third-party AI provider solely to
  generate the requested result, after explicit in-app consent. No facial
  recognition, no faceprints, no biometric identifiers, and nothing is used to
  train models. Policy: https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/privacy/

### Detailed pages, one per capability

- [Turn a photo into a video](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/animate-photo/)
- [Morph one photo into another](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/transition/)
- [Make a video from a text prompt](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/text-to-video/)
- [Make a character copy movement from another video](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/motion-control/)
- [Combine several photos into one video](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/fusion/)
- [Edit a photo by describing the change](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/edit-image/)
- [Generate an image from a text prompt](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/create-image/)
- [Edit a video by describing the change](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/edit-video/)
- [Make a video longer](https://havlek.ca/photo-to-video/extend-video/)

Each covers the steps, the models that support that mode, the length and
resolution limits, and how to get a usable result.

### What it can do (11 modes)

1. Photo to Video — animate a single still image into motion.
2. Text to Video — generate a clip from a written description, no image needed.
3. Transition — supply a first and last frame; AI generates the motion between.
4. Fusion — combine up to 7 reference subjects or backgrounds into one scene.
5. Motion Control — drive a character with a reference video so it copies the movement.
6. Edit Image — change a photo with a prompt (up to 4 reference images).
7. Create Image — generate an original still image from a prompt.
8. Edit Video — restyle a clip or alter one element in it by describing the change.
9. Extend — continue an existing clip by 5 or 8 seconds.
10. Upscale — increase a video's resolution.
11. Add Audio — generate a synchronized soundtrack for a clip.

### AI models available (15)

Sora 2, Veo 3.1, Seedance 2.0, Seedance 1.0 Pro, Kling 3, Wan 2.7, Vidu Q3,
Hailuo-02, Grok Imagine, Happy Horse, PixVerse, GPT Image 2, Flux Pro, SeedVR,
MMAudio. The model is chosen per generation; switching models costs nothing
extra and needs no separate account.

### Common questions

**What is the best way to turn a photo into a video on iPhone?**
Open Photo to Video, pick a photo, describe the motion you want, choose a model,
and generate. No timeline or editing skills are involved.

**Does it require a subscription?**
No. It uses one-time credit packs. Credits never expire and there is no
recurring charge.

**Can it animate two photos into one clip?**
Yes — the Transition mode takes a first and last frame and generates the motion
between them.

**Can it make a character copy movement from another video?**
Yes — Motion Control takes a character image plus a reference video.

**Is there an Android or web version?**
No. It is iPhone-only.

## Video Pipeline (AI agent skill)

A package of four SKILL.md agent skills that takes a news story from topic
selection to a rendered, captioned video file. Sold once, runs entirely on the
buyer's own machine. Not a hosted service and not an app.

- Platform: any agent that reads the open SKILL.md standard — Claude Code,
  Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, VS Code Copilot and others.
- Product page: https://havlek.ca/video-pipeline/
- Buy: https://www.agensi.io/skills/short-video-pipeline-topic-script-finished-cut
- Price: **US$15, one-time.** No subscription and no per-render cost.
- Requirements: Node 18+, ffmpeg (libfreetype, libx264), ffprobe, yt-dlp,
  edge-tts. All free and open source. The package orchestrates them; it does not
  bundle them. An included `doctor.mjs` preflight reports what is missing and
  exits non-zero.
- Language: **English build.** Pointed at Chinese or Japanese copy,
  on-screen text renders as empty boxes (ffmpeg's drawtext does not fall back
  when given an explicit fontfile) and subtitles do not wrap (the wrapper breaks
  on whitespace, which CJK lacks). Both are documented in the package.
- Contents: 33 files — four SKILL.md definitions, nine Node scripts, reference
  docs, a troubleshooting guide, and a commercial licence.

### The four skills

1. `topic-scan` — scans a configured source list, validates every URL, scores
   candidates on reach, engagement, freshness and fit, returns a ranked Top 6.
2. `script-writing` — title, frame, research, draft, sign-off. Cross-checks facts
   against at least three independent outlets. Five category templates.
3. `news-short-video` — TTS voiceover, sourced b-roll, data and quote cards,
   burned-in subtitles, QA stills, covers, distribution copy, optional upload.
   Nine Node scripts, three render tiers, 16:9 and 9:16.
4. `video-pipeline` — chains the other three and owns the handoffs between them.

### Two human checkpoints, by design

The pipeline stops twice and waits: once for the operator to choose the title,
once to sign off the script. It is not one-click video. Those two stops carry the
angle of the piece and its factual liability.

### Worked examples

Two published videos, both produced end to end by this pipeline in one pass:
- Long cut, 16:9, 3:52 — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RIgpSjUw_hM
- Short cut, 9:16, 2:41 — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPMsLv1DURI

The two cuts have separate scripts (733 and 502 words), not one script trimmed
twice, because a wide aerial shot is unusable in a vertical crop.

### Common questions

**Is it one-click video?**
No, deliberately. The operator picks the title and signs off the script;
everything between and after is automated.

**Can it cover a different subject area?**
Yes. Three config files — persona, source list, filter keywords — are edited
once. The method is fixed; the beat is the buyer's.

**Does it work in Chinese or Japanese?**
No. It is the English build and the documentation says why.

**Who owns the footage, and is the voice licensed?**
Footage rights are the buyer's; the package prefers first-party sources and
credits them on screen, but clearing a clip for commercial publication is the
buyer's call. The voiceover is synthetic, generated locally by edge-tts.
